notes: The soaks that crashed while working (r-next10 and r-next15, 15-17-10-2026): Qwen3-32B at
32 requests on one GCD, with Q4_K_M or Q8_0 weights and an f16 or q8_0 KV cache, aborted
hours into a soak, and one Qwen3-30B-A3B Q8_0 server met a GPU memory fault
(HSA_STATUS_ERROR_MEMORY_APERTURE_VIOLATION). The runner of those rounds counted the soaks
as passed, since fewer than half of their requests failed. The same configurations again,
on an engine that stops cleanly (next17) and a runner that records a server that dies
(servers_died, server_exits), with llama.cpp's own log on, so that a crash leaves the line
that says why. Qwen3-14B Q8_0 with a q8_0 KV cache, which did not crash, as control.
One GCD a point: six of them share a node, each stretching to the time the job has, up to
six hours.
First pass (next17, 18-19-10-2026): all five ran their six hours, none died, and every
server stopped with 0. Six hours was too short: the soaks of c01 died 8 to 11.5 hours in.
The long groups run the same configurations 12 to 16 hours, the Qwen3-32B ones twice
(a copy is the same point in a group of another name), eight GCDs: one node.
Second pass (19-20-10-2026): a long-32b server died about six hours in, on
hipGraphInstantiate: 'ROCm error: out of memory' in ggml_cuda_graph_evaluate_and_capture,
four seconds after its sequences' logits turned NaN; its VRAM had grown, 52 GB at a
throughput point, 58-61 GB at the end of a six-hour soak. The graphs-* groups run the same
configurations three hours with llama.cpp's HIP graphs on and off
(GGML_CUDA_DISABLE_GRAPHS=1), one node, to see whether VRAM still grows without them.
Third pass (20-10-2026): in their first half hour the graphs-* servers grew 0.6-2.3 GiB
an hour with the graphs on and not at all with them off. nographs-* soaks the configurations
that died 12 to 16 hours with the graphs off; graphs-speed measures what the graphs are
worth, Qwen3-8B and Qwen3-32B at 1 to 32 requests, on and off.
